items.title: Live steps instead of dots
items.text: While yAI looks things up, the reply shows each step as it happens (Checking the weather in Waterloo, ON · Searching arXiv for …), with a tick when each is done.

items.title: Plain-words steps
items.text: Connections in yAI Code show the same words while they run, in the spinner and the step row.

items.title: Spotify and Google Drive removed
items.text: The Spotify and Google Drive and Docs connections are gone; GitHub, LEARN, webhooks, weather, maps, Wolfram Alpha, papers and YouTube stay. Google sign-in goes back to asking only for calendar and email.

items.title: Connections
items.text: yAI can now use outside services when a question needs them: live weather, maps and directions, Wolfram Alpha, arXiv and Semantic Scholar papers, YouTube transcripts, and your own GitHub, Google Drive and Docs, Spotify and UWaterloo LEARN due dates. Open Connections in the account menu to connect them. Answers say which ones were used, with sources.

items.title: Actions wait for you
items.text: Anything that changes something (a Spotify playlist, a GitHub issue, a Google Doc, a webhook message) comes as a card with a Do it button, and only happens when you press it.

items.title: Webhooks
items.text: Save webhooks (Discord, Slack, Zapier, n8n, any URL) under Connections. yAI can send to them, and scheduled tasks can send their results there too. Scheduled tasks also use your connected services, so "every Sunday, tell me what is due on LEARN" works.

items.title: Connections in the terminal
items.text: The same services reach yAI Code through its service tool. New commands: /connections, /pr (push and open a pull request written from the diff), /issues (pick a GitHub issue and let yAI work on it) and /deploy (a Vercel preview or production, with a fix offer if the build fails).

items.title: /team plans the layout first
items.text: The lead now plans every file and its owner up front. yAI makes the folders before anyone starts, and every agent gets the whole map in its brief.

items.title: Live previews no longer stop at "Script error"
items.text: Code that saves data (localStorage) or uses cookies now runs in the preview, the way it does when opened in the browser. Errors from scripts loaded from the big CDNs show the real message and line instead of "Script error.".

items.title: No verdict is a warning
items.text: In /team, a checker that finishes without its verdict now shows "no verdict" in yellow with a warning that its check may be incomplete, and the fixer gets its report to look at.

items.title: yAI re-runs the tests after the fixer
items.text: When the fixer is done, yAI runs the test commands the team used (or npm test) itself and shows the real result next to the fixer's verdict, with a warning if it said FIXED but the tests still fail. The fixer is also told to quote each check it ran with its result.

items.title: Open any agent in /team
items.text: While a team works, press an agent's number on the board, or click its row, to watch it live: what it says, each step and its result, and its file edits as coloured diffs. Esc goes back to the board (Esc on the board still stops the team).

items.title: /team log
items.text: After a team finishes, /team log 2 (or /team log tester) prints that agent's whole log into the conversation.

releases.title: Copy and paste in yAI Code

items.title: Select to copy
items.text: Drag over any text in yAI Code to select it; it is copied when you let go, as in Claude Code. A selection stays inside the conversation or the plan panel, and wrapped lines come back together.

items.title: Pasting
items.text: Pasted text no longer sends the prompt at its line breaks. A short line goes in as typed; anything longer shows as [Pasted text #1 +N lines] and the whole text goes to the model.

items.title: /team questions stay on screen
items.text: When a team agent asks to run a command, its question no longer flashes and disappears: the live board waits until you answer.

items.title: Tester, reviewer, security checker, docs writer and fixer in /team
items.text: After the builders finish, the members you picked check the work together: the integration agent (do the pieces fit), a tester (writes and runs tests), a reviewer (bugs and edge cases), a security checker and a docs writer. Each ends with a verdict. If any of them finds a problem, the fixer runs last with their reports, fixes it and re-runs the checks; if nothing is found it is skipped.

items.title: Choose who is on the team
items.text: After the lead splits the task, a checklist shows the builders and every role: tick or untick with space or a number, then Start. Your picks are remembered for next time. The verdicts are summed up in one line when the team finishes.

items.title: Searches the web when it needs to
items.text: Without pressing Search, yAI checks whether your question needs the web (news, prices, anything recent or obscure, or when you ask it to look something up) and searches on its own, with sources as usual. Coding, maths and writing questions go straight to the answer.

items.title: Yolo mode
items.text: Shift+Tab now also offers auto-accept everything: edits, commands and deletions run without asking (/mode yolo). In /team the builders follow it too.

items.title: An integration agent in /team
items.text: After the agents finish, an integration agent checks, read-only, that their pieces fit together: imports exist, names and routes match, nothing is left half-wired. Its verdict comes last in the report.

items.title: A plan you can trust
items.text: The plan's progress now counts finished steps, not tool calls, never goes backwards, and is complete when a task ends well.

items.title: Ultra Flash tool calls
items.text: yAI Ultra Flash now writes its tool calls in its own native format, so steps are no longer thrown away as unfinished.

items.title: No more jumping screen
items.text: Typing (backspace included) only redraws what changed, inside one update, and nothing touches the window's last column, so a wide symbol can't push a row over and make the whole screen jump.

items.title: /team tidies up
items.text: The agents' board no longer comes back under the reports after the team is done.

items.title: Resizing
items.text: After the window gets narrower, boxes and right-aligned rows are cut at the edge instead of breaking into pieces.

releases.title: yAI Code asks before it guesses

items.title: Questions in a small form
items.text: When a task has real choices the code can't answer (a fixed list or free text? one field or several?), yAI asks up to four questions in a form: a tab for each, numbered options with a line under each, Type something for your own answer, and Chat about this to talk it over. The Submit tab shows your answers before they go.

items.title: A full-window app, like the design
items.text: The header with the status pill stays at the top, the plan sits in a panel on the right while yAI works, and the input box and the keys that work right now stay at the bottom. PgUp/PgDn or the mouse wheel scroll back through the conversation. YAI_CLASSIC=1 brings back the plain scrolling terminal.

items.title: Ready to type straight away
items.text: MCP servers start in the background, so the input works at once; a message waits for them if it needs their tools.

items.title: Cleaner start
items.text: The start screen sits in the middle of the window and gives way to the conversation; "pick up where you left off" shows a clean title.

items.title: Always know what it is doing
items.text: A status pill says Ready, Working, Finished or Needs attention, and while yAI works its plan stays at the bottom with each step ticked off and the files it changed.

items.title: Plain-language start
items.text: Instead of a wall of tips: what yAI saw in the project and four starters (fix something, add a feature, explain the project, review changes), each a single key, and R to pick up the last conversation.

items.title: One-key answers
items.text: Approvals say what a command does and how risky it is (read-only, changes files, network, risky) and take y, a or n. When a task is done you get a summary and r, c or u to review, commit or undo it all.

items.title: Failures in plain words
items.text: When a test fails, yAI explains it simply before the stack trace and offers f to fix it, s to see the fix first, or n to leave it.

items.title: Commands with descriptions
items.text: Typing / shows matching commands with what each does and what is on now; arrows move, tab completes, and the bar under the input lists the keys that work right now.

items.title: Hosted models labelled right
items.text: yAI Q3.8 Max now shows as Hosted in the model picker.

items.title: Opens on the logo
items.text: The phone app opens on the yAI logo, which settles in while your chats load, then fades into the app.

items.title: A bigger start screen
items.text: The start box shows yAI in large letters with the version and tagline on one line, like the videos.

items.title: /team: agents that split the work
items.text: A lead splits the task into 2 to 4 parts that touch different files, and the agents do them at the same time while a live board shows each one's step, time and cost. Commands still ask you first. Their reports land in your conversation.

items.title: Fewer failed steps with yAI Ultra Flash
items.text: In long sessions Ultra Flash sometimes wrote its tool calls slightly wrong (a missing quote), so steps failed with "a path is required" and had to be redone. Those calls are now understood the first time.

items.title: Model arena removed
items.text: The arena and its leaderboard are gone; the phone app has three tabs: Chats, Projects and You.

items.title: Diagrams, charts and formulas
items.text: Charts and diagrams redraw in the right colours when you switch light or dark, wide diagrams stay readable on a phone, and a long formula shows a shadow where it scrolls.

items.title: No more surprise keyboard
items.text: Turning on a tool from the + menu (search, deep research, study, canvas) or tapping a start suggestion no longer pops the keyboard; only tapping the message box does.

items.title: Tidier layouts
items.text: Wide diagrams stay readable and scroll sideways, long project names are cut off neatly instead of wrapping, and the theme buttons are easier to tap.

items.title: Scheduled tasks
items.text: Tell yAI to do something every day, on weekdays, every week or once, at a time you pick (for example a morning news briefing with web search). Each result is saved as a chat marked ⏰ and sent to your phone or browser as a notification. Find it under Scheduled in the sidebar.

items.title: Diagrams and charts in answers
items.text: When a picture explains it better, answers include diagrams (flows, sequences, timelines) and charts (bar, line, area, pie, scatter) with a table view and a download button.

items.title: Prompt caching
items.text: The repeated part of a conversation is cached by the model, so follow-up messages are faster and cost up to 80% less from your daily allowance. Your usage page shows the tokens served from cache.

items.title: Fits your window
items.text: Resizing the terminal redraws at the new width, and file searches and reads show a spinner with a timer.

releases.title: A much bigger yAI Q3.8 Max

items.title: yAI Q3.8 Max is now Qwen3.8 Max
items.text: The 2.4-trillion-parameter Qwen3.8 Max replaces the 27B model. It answers right away instead of waiting for a cloud GPU to wake, and like yAI Ultra it counts toward your daily allowance (about half of Ultra's price). It reads text only; for images use yAI Ultra or yAI Ultra Flash.

releases.title: yAI on your phone, as an app

items.title: Three tabs
items.text: Chats, Projects and You, with the tabs out of the way inside a conversation.

items.title: Sheets for models and tools
items.text: Tap the model under the chat title to switch, and + for Camera, Photos, Files, Search, Research, Image, Video, Study, Canvas and Voice.

items.title: Feels native
items.text: Swipe from the left edge or use your phone's back button to go back, a full-screen live preview, and a Settings screen with Light, Dark or System theme.

items.title: yAI Ultra Flash
items.text: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: fast, reads images, no GPU to wake, and about a tenth of yAI Ultra's price per word. It shares yAI Ultra's daily allowance, so the same dollars go about ten times further.

items.title: Voice mode
items.text: Speak instead of typing with the mic, press Listen under any answer, or start a hands-free voice chat. Natural voices when the site has them, your browser's voice otherwise.

items.title: Canvas
items.text: Long writing and code open in an editor beside the chat. Edit by hand, select a part and ask yAI to change it, step through versions, and run HTML, JavaScript and Python live.

items.title: Search your chats
items.text: Ctrl K (⌘K on a Mac) searches every chat's messages, and jumps to the exact message. New chat moved to Ctrl Shift O.

items.title: Study mode
items.text: A tutor that gives hints and asks questions instead of handing over answers (Tools > Study mode), plus a Study page with flashcards (spaced repetition) and practice quizzes made from your notes, PDFs or chats.

items.title: Calendar and email
items.text: Connect Google to ask about your week and your inbox. yAI suggests Gmail drafts and calendar events; nothing is saved until you press the button.

items.title: Better image editing
items.text: An Edit button on every image yAI makes, one-tap ideas (remove the background, watercolor, winter...), and a before/after slider.

items.title: Install yAI as an app
items.text: Account menu > Install the app (or Add to Home Screen on an iPhone). It opens full screen with its own icon.

items.title: Public API keys
items.text: Call yAI's models from your own code with an OpenAI-style API at /v1, under your own daily limits. Keys are on the API keys page.

items.title: VS Code extension, /resume, plan approval
items.text: yAI Code in a VS Code side panel with changes shown as diffs; /resume picks any earlier session; plan mode ends with a plan you approve.

items.title: Live cost, /compact, image to code, run from your phone
items.text: The status line shows what yAI Ultra has cost this session and today; /compact takes a focus; /clone rebuilds a page from a screenshot; yai remote takes tasks from your phone.

items.title: People and limits
items.text: Admins see everyone's use, change each person's daily limits, pause accounts, and get automatic flags for unusual use.

releases.title: Data analysis, deep research and memory

items.title: Data analysis
items.text: Attach a CSV, Excel or JSON file; Python runs in your browser and the charts show in the chat.

items.title: Deep research
items.text: Several rounds of searching and reading, then a report with sources.

items.title: Memory
items.text: yAI remembers lasting facts you tell it; edit them in Account > Memory.

items.title: Paste screenshots and /usage
items.text: Alt+V pastes a screenshot into the prompt; /usage shows today's limits.

items.title: A new look
items.text: New colours and type, a sidebar that folds into a rail, and a new usage page.

items.title: yAI Code redesign
items.text: Dark and light themes, a start screen, step rows, diffs and arrow-key approvals.

items.title: New model names
items.text: yAI Ultra, yAI Q3.8 Max, yAI 3 Coder, yAI Q3.5 and yAI P4.

items.title: Search the web
items.text: Answers with numbered sources.

items.title: Projects
items.text: Files and instructions shared by every chat in a project.

items.title: Live previews
items.text: Run the HTML and JavaScript yAI writes, right in the chat.

items.title: Usage page
items.text: See what you've used.
